A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Cut Cross-Entropy research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support matching retained material against additions and revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original runtime and memory measurements, component ablations, and Alpaca fine-tuning loss curves, including additional model benchmarks in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original runtime, memory, and fine-tuning results, plus OpenWebText pretraining validation curves, component profiling, and batch-size sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: v2 adds Kahan compensated summation and variants that disable filtering for classifier or embedding gradients. CCE-Kahan-FullC changes the backward procedure specifically to address pretraining failures. The original tiled computation remains; Algorithm 4 additionally documents the fused backward pass already described in v1.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates training stability through Alpaca instruction fine-tuning. v2 retains Alpaca and adds OpenWebText pretraining with held-out validation, substantially extending the represented data and training scenario.

E2.justification: The external baselines remain Liger Kernels, Torch Tune, torch.compile, and plain PyTorch. Tables 1 and A1 add CCE-Kahan, CCE-Kahan-FullC, and CCE-Kahan-FullE as evaluated comparison variants; the additional-model runtime table also includes CCE-Kahan-FullC.

E3.justification: v2 introduces training on 5% of OpenWebText, nonoverlapping 0.25% validation, and validation perplexity, alongside batch-size sweeps and component-timing procedures. Figure 4 replaces Llama 3 8B with Qwen 2.5 7B; the runtime benchmarks replace Llama with Qwen 2.5 7B and add 32B. These are evaluation changes beyond additional setting disclosures.

E4.justification: v2 adds numerical-precision variants and selective-filtering ablations, backward-component profiling in Table A2, and batch-size sensitivity analyses in Figures A1–A2. These investigate precision costs and runtime bottlenecks beyond v1's filtering/sorting ablations. The ignored-token analysis is retained after relocation.

E5.justification: Both versions report five-seed averages and 95% confidence intervals for fine-tuning curves. v2 newly states five-seed averaging for the existing runtime/memory tables and uses it for new experiments. This establishes expanded reporting, not an explicit increase in runs for retained experiments.

E6.justification: Under Table 1's same reported A100/8,192-token setting, CCE loss-plus-gradient time changes from 135 to 145 ms, versus 143 ms for torch.compile in both versions, reversing their ranking. Appendix measurements and Figure 4 curves also change. New results include pretraining perplexity parity and a reported 16% Mistral NeMo training-time reduction with doubled batch size. Figure 1's underlying memory estimates remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 4.3 revises transpose placement in the gradient equations, including changing the explicit identities' left-hand sides from gradients to transposed gradients, matching Algorithm 3's presentation. This is a localized mathematical revision. The loss decomposition and filtering argument remain; the new notation and floating-point appendices mainly explain existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Discussion retain the central claims of negligible cross-entropy memory overhead without sacrificing training speed or convergence. The new experiments and qualifications do not revise these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2 identifies two pretraining failure mechanisms absent from v1: suppressing classifier gradients for poorly supported tokens and precision loss during gradient accumulation. It distinguishes fine-tuning from pretraining requirements and explains how temporary-buffer reuse and larger batches can offset the corrected variant's costs. Appendix C also adds explanations of runtime bottlenecks.

D1.justification: v2 adds full fused-backward pseudocode, discloses the gradient accumulation precision, and specifies memory-accounting formulas and storage assumptions in Appendix D. These improve implementation and calculation transparency. The code-access link and existing A100, PyTorch, and CUDA disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Related Work gains a paragraph on sequence and model parallelism, citing Jacobs, Li, and Shoeybi. References for Kahan summation, OpenWebText, and Qwen 2.5 are also added. The positioning relative to attention implementations and efficient cross-entropy baselines remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the analysis, separates fine-tuning and pretraining discussion, expands explanatory material, and reorganizes the appendices around notation, performance, memory accounting, and floating-point addition. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain intact; the header changes to ICLR 2025 publication status.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5, the extensive runtime plots in Figures A1–A2, a profiling table, a notation table, and Algorithm 4. Figure 4 is replotted with different axes and a replacement model, while performance tables gain variant rows. The original raw memory table is retained and relocated from Table A3 to A4.

improvement.justification: v1's convergence evidence covered fine-tuning while its claims were broader. v2 identifies consequential pretraining failures, introduces a targeted correction, and supplies held-out perplexity evidence across four models in Figure 5. Profiling and batch-size analyses further clarify practical tradeoffs. The corrected variant costs more memory and computation, and timing prose still contains inconsistencies with tables, but diagnosing and addressing this important applicability gap substantially improves the paper.
